tx.f.keine_prevouts: The input amounts are missing: this node cannot look up the transactions they came from, because it keeps no transaction index or has been pruned. Fee and input total therefore stay open.
tx.f.nachfahren: {n} unconfirmed descendants hang off it; together they pay {rate} sat/vB and are mined together.
tx.f.nachfahren_1: One unconfirmed descendant hangs off it; together they pay {rate} sat/vB and are mined together.
tx.f.offen: It is not in a block yet.
tx.f.opreturn: One output carries no payment but {b} bytes of data written into the blockchain.
tx.f.opreturn_text: One output carries no payment but {b} bytes of data: {text}
tx.f.perzentil_hoch: At {rate} sat/vB it paid more than nine out of ten transactions in its block.
tx.f.perzentil_mitte: At {rate} sat/vB it sat in the middle of its block, whose median was {median} sat/vB.
tx.f.perzentil_niedrig: At {rate} sat/vB it paid less than nine out of ten transactions in its block — it got in cheaply.
tx.f.raus_geflogen: It sits close to the mempool's minimum fee ({min} sat/vB). If traffic rises, it is among the first to be evicted.
tx.f.rbf_ererbt: It does not signal replaceability itself, but it hangs off an unconfirmed ancestor that does — so it can be replaced anyway.
tx.f.rbf_ja: This transaction signals that it may be replaced.
tx.f.rbf_nein: It does not signal replaceability. Do not rely on that: many nodes now accept a replacement without the signal.
tx.f.reicht: At the current level of traffic its fee is enough for a confirmation within about {n} blocks.
tx.f.reicht_naechster: At the current level of traffic its fee is enough for the next block.
tx.f.reicht_nicht: Its fee is below every estimate this node makes — even for a wait of {n} blocks it reckons {rate} sat/vB.
tx.f.segwit: SegWit: its witness data is {b} bytes but counts as only {v} vbytes, saving it {s} vbytes of block space.
tx.f.sperrzeit_folgenlos: It carries a locktime, but every one of its sequence numbers is final, which leaves that locktime without effect.
tx.f.sperrzeit_hoehe: It could not become valid before block {h}.
tx.f.teils_weg: {n} of its {gesamt} outputs have already been spent again.
tx.f.teils_weg_1: One of its {gesamt} outputs has already been spent again.
tx.f.unterwegs: {n} outputs are being passed on right now, in transactions that are not confirmed yet.
tx.f.unterwegs_1: One output is being passed on right now, in a transaction that is not confirmed yet.
tx.f.unverbreitet: This node has not handed it on to anyone yet — it probably originated right here.
tx.f.verteilung: It pays {n} recipients at once — that is what a payout batch looks like.
tx.f.verwaist: It sits in a block that is no longer part of the longest chain, so it counts as unconfirmed.
tx.f.wartet: It has been waiting in the mempool for {dauer}.
tx.f.wechselgeld: Output {n} has the same script type as the inputs. Often, though not always, that is the change coming back.
tx.f.wiederverwendung: One output pays back to the very script it just spent from. That links both payments together in public.
tx.f.zu_billig: At {rate} sat/vB it is below what the last {n} blocks have been charging ({min} sat/vB), so it may sit for a long while.
tx.f.zu_viele_eltern: With {n} inputs, looking every predecessor up one by one would put more load on your node than this page is worth. The input amounts therefore stay open.
tx.f.zusammenlegung: It sweeps {n} inputs into a single output — that is tidying up, not paying someone.
tx.locktime.inert: without effect — every input is final
tx.miss.notxid: That is not a transaction ID. A transaction ID is exactly 64 hexadecimal characters long.
tx.miss.notxindex: Your node keeps no transaction index, and this transaction is not waiting in the mempool either. Without that index it can only look up what is currently pending. Add txindex=1 to your bitcoin.conf and let it build once; after that Satscope finds every transaction there has ever been.
tx.miss.title: Transaction not found
tx.miss.unknown: Your node does not know this transaction: it is neither waiting in the mempool nor in any block it holds.
tx.miss.unreachable: Your node did not answer. Nothing can be looked up while it stays silent.
tx.title: Transaction
xpub.chain_empty: Not one address of this branch has ever been used.
xpub.empty: Not one address of this key has ever been used. Either the wallet is new, or the coins sit under a different derivation.
xpub.gap: Stopped after {n} unused addresses in a row — the rule every wallet follows.
xpub.incomplete: The index did not answer for every address. What is missing shows a dash; nothing has been guessed, and the total may be too low.
xpub.local: This key stays on your node. Nothing about it is sent anywhere.
xpub.nf.form: That is not an extended public key. They are 111 characters long and begin with xpub, ypub or zpub.
xpub.nf.intern: Satscope could not build the addresses for this key. It shows nothing rather than something wrong.
xpub.nf.mehrsig: {v} belongs to a multisig wallet. Its addresses are made from several keys at once, so they cannot be derived from this one alone.
xpub.nf.privat: That is a PRIVATE key — whoever reads it can spend the coins. Satscope has not stored it and does not show it here. Treat those coins as exposed and move them to a wallet whose key nobody has seen.
xpub.nf.title: Not a usable key
xpub.nf.version: Version {v} is not one Satscope knows.
xpub.noindex: No Electrum index answered, so there are no balances. The addresses themselves are exact — they were derived here, not looked up.
xpub.strip_alt: One column per address, index 0 on the left; the height is its balance
xpub.testnet: A testnet key. The addresses are exact, but they are not looked up: this node's index holds the real chain.
xpub.title: Extended public key
xpub.truncated: Stopped at {n} addresses. This wallet goes further — what lies beyond is not counted here.
